values: Titanium Model B: data and feature guide
1,188 rows; January 2010-June 2026; one row per month and supplier group. Six groups: USA, Japan, France, Russia, China and Other.
Country supply-share movement probabilities: collapse, fall, stable and rise. Required horizons are 3 and 6 months; H12 is additional reporting. It does not predict a titanium price.
75 fields exist in the training CSV. Original model: 35 input features. Improved model: 66 input features, including 26 extra fields computed in memory during training.

The input CSV is already processed. "In upstream prepared CSV?" means the exact field name exists in the preceding trade + FX + ERUC file. It does not mean the field came directly from a raw download, or was copied unchanged.

UN Comtrade supplies trade values, import weights and partner information. Bank of England supplies the monthly USD-per-GBP rate. ONS supplies ERUC, a broad basic-metals import-price index. No USGS, nickel or aluminium benchmark features are used.

Currency conversion, HS aggregation, reconstructed country quantities, shares, lag changes, rolling statistics, class labels and assumed publication dates are processing results. The Field guide records each calculation.
Filter Original model role or Improved model role to "Yes - predictor". These are the fields passed into the estimator. Other columns support calculations, timing checks, labels or display.
Original H3/H6/H12 models learn target_class_h3/h6/h12. Improved H3 learns target_class_h3; selected improved H6/H12 regressors learn target_share_change_h6/h12, then produce class probabilities.

Columns starting target_ contain future observed outcomes or their metadata. They are labels or audit controls, not predictor inputs. Recent rows have blank targets because the future month has not been observed.
A share of 0.10 means 10% of imported weight. A share change of +0.02 means +2 percentage points. It is different from a 2% relative increase.

ln(current/past) is a natural-log change. For small movements it approximates relative percentage change; the exact fraction is exp(log change)-1. Supplier quantity uses ln(1+kg) so zero quantities remain valid.
Share change < -0.144608: collapse; below -0.022945: fall; through 0.020887: stable; above that: rise. Boundaries use pooled H3 changes with targets through June 2021, starting in 2010.

Historical lag fields need prior months. Future target fields need later observations. Missing counts on the field tabs are counts in the entire loaded dataset, not counts in a particular training fold.

The Feature influence tab shows the original selected tree models' saved relative importances. Larger values mean greater use in those fitted models. They do not prove causation, indicate a positive/negative effect, or guarantee forecast accuracy.

Original H3/H12 use Random Forest; H6 uses Extra Trees. The saved scores are impurity-based tree importance, normalized to 100% per horizon. The six one-hot country_key scores are summed back into one field. Rows are sorted by mean H3/H6 importance.

The improved experiment saves permutation scores, measured as a change in an accuracy score. Those scores are not percentages comparable with the original tree importance. Its saved analysis uses recent rows also seen by the final fitted models, so it is descriptive rather than independent test evidence.

Trade unit value reflects the imported product mix. ERUC is broad metals inflation. Country quantities are reconstructed from upstream shares and HS weights. "Other" groups countries together, affecting concentration and ranking features.
Definitions were checked against the preparation and training code, feature manifests, frozen thresholds, the training CSV and saved original importance scores. Recorded on 8 October 2026.
